round4_design.produced_by: head of staff: 3 analyst pods in parallel (engine internals, benchmark instrument, front page) -> coordinator re-derived the load-bearing measurement -> design
round4_design.finding: The 18 defects reduce to 2 root causes: (A) strength is an accumulator written by five code paths and 'is this the same memory?' is answered twice by two different rules - D1, D9, D13, D14, D17 + W2/W3; (B) a benchmark record has no declared shape and a run has no declared scope - D2-D8, D15, D16.
mechanism: Rule 1 - strength is derived, never accumulated: strength()/realize() with (score, score_at), tier computed; idempotent, so refresh frequency stops being semantic (D1 dies by construction)

Rule 2 - one classifier, three policies: unrelated | duplicate | update, shared by the write path and the boundary pass; a retired memory is never a merge target (D13/D14 die) and a value-changing update is detectable with no retire signal - the only mechanism proposed that can move the decay-only leak off 1.000
Rule 3 - one index version, one pass: _touch/_ensure_index on every mutator, consolidate() as the only rebuild site; the rebuild leaves the query path (W2) and _cluster()/mem.cluster are deleted (W3)

measured_coupling.why: the decay fix is not local - it changes how many memories render at full length, which is the input to the budget-efficiency claim
measured_coupling.method: model of the engine's own scoring, validated against the shipped engine, re-run with the fixed decay rule; 900-memory scale corpus, seed 0, 60 virtual days
measured_coupling.consequence: criterion 1 (budget efficiency, PASS today at 1589 vs 1734) is at risk from the decay fix alone, so the fix must land together with a re-swept tier policy (thresholds + rendering caps + DETAIL_VALUE) and a diversity term in the packer

arms.M3t: BM25 rank + common.downgrade() truncation - the first caller that unused function would ever have
arms.M3p: BM25 rank + the engine's detail ladder: is the allocator the win?
arms.M3k: BM25 rank + the engine's value-per-char packer with utility = rank position: is the packer the win?
arms.M11: engine cosine with PRIOR_WEIGHT=0 on hold-out seeds 3-4: is the retrieval-strength prior a cost to ranking?
arms.M12: engine cosine with the unified mechanism: does the store still add anything, and can it move the decay-only leak?

round4_design.first_slice: realize() + _touch/_ensure_index (~30 lines, testable with test_engine.py alone): realize() twice at the same now is a no-op, N daily realisations equal INITIAL_SCORE x exp(-rate x N) to 1e-9, and incremental index state equals a full rebuild after any add/access/retire/pin sequence
round4_design.landing_rule: the whole mechanism ships as a labelled 11th arm (M12); the (score, score_at) migration is a labelled protocol change with a load() shim, and D13's change in stored counts is never compared across the change (BM-002 / BM-006)

board_meetings.trigger: Disagreement on how to satisfy 'beat semantic memory' without rigging the test

positions.engineering: Bake query similarity into engine.recall(); the hybrid is the product.
positions.research: That silently redefines the claim. A spec-faithful engine must stay measurable separately or the result is unattributable.
positions.product: Ship the version that performs, and say plainly which configuration is recommended.

board_meetings.verdict: Keep BOTH. M6 pure remains the spec-faithful baseline; improvements ship as named ablation arms M7-M10.

board_meetings.trigger: Staleness is a product capability, not a decay fix

positions.product: Add explicit supersession; that is what actually retires a stale fact.
positions.research: Supersession is a new feature. It does not demonstrate that decay retires stale facts; report them separately or drop the claim.
positions.engineering: Both are cheap; measure them as two distinct metrics.

board_meetings.verdict: Implement supersession AND report decay-only staleness as its own number. Never present a supersession win as a decay win.
board_meetings.outcome: Upheld by the data: supersession leaks 0.000, decay-only leaks 1.000.

board_meetings.trigger: The pre-registered hero arm M10 measured WORSE than M8/M9 after the run

positions.engineering: Swap the hero to M8; it is the configuration we would actually recommend.
positions.research: Swapping the hero after seeing the numbers is exactly what pre-registration exists to prevent.
positions.product: Report both: keep the pre-registered arm honest and name the best configuration explicitly.

board_meetings.verdict: The hero stays M10 at its measured value. The report adds a separate, clearly-labelled criterion for the best measured configuration (M8). No post-hoc swapping.

board_meetings.trigger: Supersession could be wired so that only the engine honours the retire signal

positions.engineering: Only the engine has versioning; baselines have nothing to do with a retire event.
positions.research: Then the staleness 'win' is an artifact of the harness, not a result.
positions.product: An unfair win is worse than a loss; it destroys the benchmark's credibility.

board_meetings.verdict: Every arm is offered the retire signal and every baseline honours it by deleting. Supersession is therefore explicitly reported as NOT an engine advantage, and the decay-only suite carries the real question.

board_meetings.trigger: The decay path compounds (arithmetic bug) - fix silently or treat as a protocol change?

positions.engineering: Fix it and move on; it is a one-line delta.
positions.research: It invalidates every decay-dependent number in rounds 1-2, including the R7 gist decision that was made because everything decayed to archived.
positions.product: A silently different decay curve with unchanged numbers is exactly how a benchmark loses credibility.

board_meetings.verdict_proposed: Fix it, label it, re-measure every decay-dependent table, and mark rounds 1-2 decay figures superseded. No silent arithmetic fix.

board_meetings.trigger: The measured 'budget efficiency win' compares the engine's packer against baselines that fill the budget with full text

positions.product: Keep the claim; it is the configuration users run.
positions.research: The two systems do not share a packer, so a packer win is unattributable to the store.
positions.engineering: The control is cheap - common.downgrade() already exists and has no callers.

board_meetings.verdict_proposed: Run the control arm (BM25 ranked, packed by the engine's allocator) first; if it matches M8, restate the win as allocation rather than store quality.

board_meetings.trigger: The significance criterion passed on one of two flat arms while the other beat the hero

positions.research: A criterion that passes if either comparator is beaten is a coin flip dressed as evidence.

board_meetings.verdict_proposed: The criterion requires BOTH flat arms to be beaten; both diffs and p-values are printed. Today the PASS is attributed to M2 while M1 flat/FIFO scored higher than the hero (0.558 vs 0.534, p=0.625).

board_meetings.trigger: The decay criterion is passable by retrieving nothing

positions.engineering: A score floor flips the leak.
positions.research: A floor trades long-horizon recall (the continuity suite asks day-0 facts at day 45) and today M0, M2 and M6 all 'pass' with hit_rate_decay_only 0.000.
positions.product: An unearnable claim should be retired, not decorated.

board_meetings.verdict_proposed: Gate every leak criterion on a retrieval floor (hit_rate_decay_only >= 0.9 x flat) and assert M0 fails it; if decay-only leak is still above 0.5 after the arithmetic fix, formally retire the 'decay retires stale facts' claim and ship contradiction-detection (auto-retire on a conflicting same-subject update) as the labelled capability instead. BM-003 said a supersession win is never a decay win; this adds the converse.

board_meetings.trigger: What may be claimed publicly after the review

positions.research: Task success is judged by an evidence-containment oracle; the top two arms differ by 0.010 (TF-IDF 0.563 vs 0.553), which is smaller than any plausible judge noise.

board_meetings.verdict_proposed: No claim ships without a supporting row in benchmarks/RESULTS.md; task-success claims are blocked until a language model judges. The 'fastest recall in the suite' wording is removed (a flat store answers in 0.60 ms p95).
